I'm reviwing this PR/code and specially this finding.
Default agent list executes every plugin twice, then may display none of them


The --all split is display-only: the default path still calls gated DiscoverAndRegister (line 83), and the filter at lines 98-103 only removes uninstalled externals from the output. Each plugin on $PATH is executed twice per invocation — info during discovery, then are-hooks-installed via GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled.


Measured agent list with external_agents: true, this branch vs main:


Plugins on PATH    main    branch
2 compiled Go plugins    0.087s    0.094s
1 Python plugin    0.084s    0.205s
9 shell-script plugins    0.05s / 0 execs    1.72s / 18 execs

In the 9-plugin case the printed output was byte-identical to main’s, because none were installed. Cost scales with plugin count x startup latency: fine for compiled plugins, material for interpreted ones (a plausible way to write an agent integration).


Context that softens this: gated DiscoverAndRegister is already on the hooks_cmd, resume, attach, explain, and review paths, so the pattern is not new. But those are not a sub-100ms listing command.


Suggested direction (design question, not a one-line fix): persist installed external agent names at agent add time so the default path can call DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways per known name instead of scanning all of $PATH. No such record exists today — EntireSettings has no installed-agents field and AreHooksInstalled is the only source of truth — which is why this needs the author’s call rather than a patch here.

Finding accurate. Here what happen:

## Two-exec chain per plugin

`entire agent list` default path (`agent_group.go:83`):

1. **`external.DiscoverAndRegister(ctx)`** → scans `$PATH` for `entire-agent-*` → each match → `registerExternalAgent` → `New()` → runs plugin's **`info`** subcommand. **Exec #1.**
2. **`GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled(ctx)`** (`config.go:86`) → loops `agent.List()`, which now includes freshly-registered externals → each → `AreHooksInstalled` → runs plugin's **`are-hooks-installed`** subcommand. **Exec #2.**

So every external plugin on `$PATH` = 2 process spawns per `list`. 9 shell plugins = 18 execs = 1.72s. Matches measurement.

## `--all` split does nothing for cost

`--all` only swaps gated discovery (`DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` vs `DiscoverAndRegister`) and the display filter at lines 99-103. **Both paths discover + exec every plugin.** Default path just filters uninstalled externals out of the *printed output* (lines 99-103) — after paying full discovery. When none installed, output byte-identical to main, yet 18 execs already burned. Work done, thrown away. Finding's "executes twice, then displays none" is correct.

## Severity — real but bounded

- Only bites when `external_agents: true` (gated discovery no-ops otherwise). Off by default.
- Cost = plugin_count × 2 × startup_latency. Compiled plugins cheap (~7ms). Interpreted (Python/shell) material — 1.7s on a sub-100ms listing command.
- Not a new pattern: gated `DiscoverAndRegister` already on hooks/resume/attach/explain/review. But those not fast listing commands. Fair distinction.

## Suggested fix — sound, needs author call

Persist installed external names at `agent add` time → default path calls `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` per known name (already exists, targets by name), skip full `$PATH` scan. Cuts default-path discovery execs to only installed plugins.

Gap finding names is real: **no installed-external record exists today.** `EntireSettings` has no such field; `AreHooksInstalled` (exec #2) is sole source of truth. So can't kill exec #1 without adding persisted state — that's schema + write-path work at `agent add`/`remove`, not a one-liner. Design decision, not inline patch. Finding correctly defers to author.

Two smaller notes if pushing back on scope:
- Even with the record, exec #2 (`AreHooksInstalled`) still runs per installed external — unavoidable, it *is* the truth source. Only exec #1 is removable.
- Cheaper partial win without new schema: skip discovery entirely on default path, list only already-registered agents — but then a hooks-installed external whose registration is missing wouldn't show. That tradeoff is the reason discovery runs. Author's call.

Eval done. Verdict: **cleaner code, but two regressions.**

## What's good
- Kills default-path double-exec. Default `list` now spawns zero external processes. Big win, matches finding's concern.
- Inlined loop reads clean, drops the `installedSet` map.

## Bug 1 — test-only agents now leak (regression)
Switched `agent.StringList()` → `agent.List()`. `StringList` filters `TestOnly` (registry.go:90); `List()` does not. Vogon (`IsTestOnly() == true`, vogon.go:48) is registered → now prints in user-facing `entire agent list`. Was hidden before. **Fix: keep filtering test-only.** Either go back to `StringList()` or skip inside loop:

```go
if to, ok := ag.(agent.TestOnly); ok && to.IsTestOnly() {
    continue
}
```
(Doing it via the `ag` you already `Get` is fine — avoids a second factory call.)

## Bug 2 — installed externals vanish from default list (breaks feature)
Default path no longer calls `DiscoverAndRegister`. Externals register **only** via runtime discovery (no persistence — finding confirmed). No global discovery hook exists — every command discovers itself (grep: attach/resume/hooks/explain each call it). So on default `agent list`, no external is registered → `agent.List()` = built-ins only. User who ran `agent add my-plugin` then `agent list` sees **nothing**. That's exactly the headline of commit `896e533` "agent list shows installed externals" — now reverted in effect.

This is the real design fork. Three options:

1. **Keep gated discovery on default path** (the branch's approach) — pay the exec cost, feature works. What the finding flagged as slow.
2. **Persist installed external names** at `agent add`, default path calls `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` per known name — fast *and* feature works. Finding's suggested direction; needs new schema field.
3. **Accept the drop** — default shows built-ins only, `--all` discovers everything. Simplest, but silently loses installed-external visibility. Must be a deliberate product call, not accident.

Your diff = option 3 by omission. If that's intended, fine — but confirm it's a choice. If the feature must stay, you need option 1 or 2.

## Open question — the `agent.Get` error
Near-unreachable. You're iterating `agent.List()` (registry keys) and immediately `Get`-ting them; only fails if the registry mutates between the two calls, and nothing in the codebase unregisters. So it's an invariant-guard, not a user-actionable condition.

`continue` = correct. But **debug, not warn** — warn implies user should act; there's nothing to do, and it'd be noise on a clean listing command. Suggest:

```go
ag, err := agent.Get(name)
if err != nil {
    logging.Debug(ctx, "agent registered but unresolvable, skipping",
        slog.String("agent", string(name)), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
    continue
}
```

Note: `AreHooksInstalled` / `AsHookSupport` don't return errors, so `Get` is the only error site — nothing else to handle.

Build clean, `types` still used. Good.

But your new complaint is the real one, and I was about to raise it. Current diff: when `external_agents` ON, default `list` shows **every** external on `$PATH` — installed *and* uninstalled. Lost the "default = installed only, `--all` = also available" distinction the branch commit promised.

## Why it happens
You dropped the display filter (old lines 99-103). To *know* an external is installed you must discover it first (register → `AreHooksInstalled`). Discovery registers uninstalled ones too, and with no filter they all print.

## Two fixes — pick by whether you also care about the exec cost

**A. Restore the filter (display-only, ~4 lines).** Keeps your clean loop, hides uninstalled externals again:

```go
isInstalled := false
if hs, ok := agent.AsHookSupport(ag); ok && hs.AreHooksInstalled(ctx) {
    isInstalled = true
    hasSomeInstalled = true
}

// Uninstalled externals are hidden unless --all. An installed external is
// only here because it was `agent add`ed, so this shows installed externals
// without listing every plugin on $PATH.
if !all && !isInstalled && external.IsExternal(ag) {
    continue
}
```

Fixes the display. **But** uninstalled plugins still get discovered (exec #1) *and* hooks-checked (exec #2), then thrown away — the finding's double-exec is untouched for `external_agents:true` users. Which, note, is the exact population the finding measured. So A makes it look right but spends the same 18 execs / 1.72s.

**B. Persist installed external names (display + perf, the finding's actual suggestion).** At `agent add`, record the name in settings; at `remove`, drop it. Default `list` then discovers **only** those names via `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` (already exists, no PATH scan of uninstalled plugins). `--all` keeps `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` to also show available ones.

Matrix under B:
| external_agents | flag | discovers | shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | default | only installed names | built-ins + installed externals |
| on | `--all` | all PATH plugins | + available externals |
| off | default | nothing | built-ins |
| off | `--all` | all PATH plugins | + available externals |

B is the only option that both hides uninstalled *and* stops exec'ing them. Cost: new settings field + write path at add/remove.

## Recommendation
You dislike the display side-effect **and** the finding was about exec cost → both arrows point at **B**. A is a band-aid that leaves the measured slowness in place. B is more work but is the durable answer.

Direct answer: **no — not for externals.**

## What exists today
- **Built-ins**: `AreHooksInstalled` reads a config file in-process (Claude: `loadClaudeSettings` → check `.claude/settings.json`, hooks.go:441). Cheap. No PATH, no exec.
- **Externals**: `AreHooksInstalled` **execs the plugin** (`are-hooks-installed`), and you can't even get the Agent object without first discovering it on PATH (glob + `info` exec). Two execs, both mandatory.
- **Persisted record**: none. Settings has only `external_agents bool` (settings.go:125). The other `agents` fields (line 351, 411) are review/loop config — unrelated. No installed-agents list anywhere. `agent add` writes hooks into the *agent's own* domain; the CLI keeps no manifest. This is exactly what the finding meant by "`AreHooksInstalled` is the only source of truth."

So the plugin binary is the sole authority on external installed-state, and reaching it costs the PATH scan you want to avoid. **To get cheap, you must add the record.** That's option B.

## Two levels of "cheap" under B

**B1 — persist names, verify by name (recommended).** At `agent add` success append name to a new settings field (`installed_external_agents []string`); at `remove` prune it. Default `list` iterates *that list* and calls `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` per name — single-binary exec, no full PATH scan. Cost scales with *installed* count (usually 1-2), not the 9 plugins on PATH. Still 2 execs per installed external, but you've killed the exec on every *uninstalled* one — the finding's actual waste.

**B2 — trust the list, zero exec.** Render ✓ straight from the persisted names, no discovery at all on default `list`. Truly zero exec. Risk: staleness — if a plugin was uninstalled out-of-band or its binary removed, the list lies until re-verified. Push verification to `--all` or a `--verify` flag.

## Recommendation
B1. It's the honest balance: display is correct (only installed externals show, no side-effect listing of all plugins) *and* cost tracks installed count instead of PATH size. B2 is cheaper but trades correctness for it — fine for a fast `list` if you accept lazy verification.

Want B1? Scope: add `installed_external_agents` to `EntireSettings` + a persist/prune helper, wire it into `agent add`/`remove`, and rewrite `runAgentList` default path to discover-by-name over the list.

Measured it — your premise needs correcting:

- **Full PATH glob (53 dirs, find `entire-agent-*`): 15 ms.** Cheap.
- **One plugin exec: ~148 ms.** × 18 = the whole 1.7–2.2s.

So **PATH is not the cost — exec'ing each discovered plugin is.** Swapping discovery mechanism buys ~15ms. The lever is *exec less / exec concurrently*, and that opens alternatives that need **no install-cache at all**.

## The hard limit (why some caching is unavoidable)
Installed-state lives *inside* the opaque plugin binary. Reading it without running it is information-theoretically impossible unless someone wrote it down — either entire writes it (manifest = the cache you want to avoid) or the plugin writes it to a standardized on-disk marker entire reads (protocol change = still a persisted record, just plugin-owned). There is no free read of an external's install-state. **Zero-exec ⇒ persisted state, always.**

But you don't need zero-exec. You need *fast*. Three cache-free levers:

## A. Parallelize the execs (biggest win, no new state)
Discovery (`discoverAndRegister`) and the `are-hooks-installed` loop are both **sequential** today. 9 plugins × 148ms serial = 1.7s. Bounded-concurrent (e.g. 8 workers) → ~1 batch ≈ 150–200ms. Zero persistence, zero protocol change. Directly kills the wall-clock.

## B. Drop the `info` exec for listing (halves exec count)
Two execs per plugin: `info` + `are-hooks-installed`. The **name is already in the filename** (`entire-agent-<name>`, parsed before any exec). `info` only supplies type/capabilities/protocol-check — a `list` doesn't need them. Exec only `are-hooks-installed`: **18 → 9 execs.** Combine with A → 9 in parallel ≈ 150ms.

(Caveat: current `registerExternalAgent` requires `info` to build the Agent object. For list you'd add a lightweight "name-only" path that skips registration and just probes install-state.)

## C. Cache `info` across runs, keyed on binary path + mtime (optional)
`info` output is stable per binary version → cacheable in the cache dir, invalidate on mtime change. `are-hooks-installed` is volatile → never cache. Removes exec #1 on warm runs without any add-time bookkeeping. This *is* a cache, but of **binary identity, not "was add called"** — it self-populates from discovery and self-invalidates on mtime. No coupling to `agent add`.

## Ranked recommendation
1. **A + B** — no persisted state, no protocol change, `list` drops ~1.7s → ~150ms. Best answer to "anything other than a cache."
2. Add **C** if you want warm runs to skip `info` too.
3. Persisted manifest (the add-cache) only if you insist on **zero** exec — and even then you'd still verify names or accept staleness.

Honest bottom line: don't replace PATH discovery (it's 15ms); make the *execs* concurrent and fewer. That gets you most of the win with none of the add-time cache you're trying to dodge.

Two separate execs, two different reasons — and for a *list*, neither is truly load-bearing.

## `info` exec — because externals are opaque and self-describing
Entire keeps **no static table** of an external plugin's identity/capabilities. The whole plugin protocol is "ask the binary": `info` returns name, type, description, capabilities, `hook_names`, `protected_dirs`. A built-in doesn't exec because its code is compiled in — entire already knows it. An external is a black box on PATH, so `New()` runs `info` to learn what it is.

**But for `list` you don't need it.** The name is in the filename — `entire-agent-<name>` — and discovery *already* parses it (`TrimPrefix(cleanName, binaryPrefix)`) *before* exec. The displayed list name is that filename-derived key, not `info.Name`. Type/capabilities aren't shown in `list`. So the `info` exec buys the list nothing. It's needed for *using* an agent (hooks, capabilities), not for naming it.

## `are-hooks-installed` exec — because we delegate install-state to the plugin
The plugin owns where and how it writes its hooks. Entire doesn't know that location, so to answer "installed?" it asks the binary. That's the ✓ marker's only source today.

**But entire orchestrates the install itself** — `install-hooks` is called *by* entire (setup.go:1622). So entire is in the loop at install time and could record the fact then, instead of interrogating the binary later. Asking the plugin every `list` is a choice, not a necessity.

## So, why exec? Because of two design choices, not a hard requirement:
1. We **reconstruct identity by asking** rather than reading the filename we already parsed.
2. We treat the plugin as **sole authority on its own install-state** rather than recording the install we performed.

Drop choice 1 → `info` exec gone from `list` (name from filename). 18→9.
Drop choice 2 → `are-hooks-installed` exec gone too, but that requires persisting the install (a marker entire drops at install, deleted at remove). Which is the persisted-state you keep circling — because, again, zero-exec install-state *must* be written down somewhere.

The honest split: the **`info` exec is pure waste on `list` and removable for free.** The **`are-hooks-installed` exec is only removable by persisting the install** — no way around it, since only the binary or a record knows.

Cheapest correct combo with no persistence: **skip `info` (name from filename) + parallelize the 9 `are-hooks-installed` execs** → ~150–200ms, still live-accurate, no cache.

## What this means
Post-skip-info, the cost driver is **PATH plugin count, not installed count**. Even with just 1 of 9 installed, you still pay 9 `are-hooks-installed` execs — because you must probe *every* discovered plugin to learn *which* is the installed one.

| user's setup | execs on default `list` |
|---|---|
| 0 plugins on PATH (typical user) | **0** — glob only, ~15ms |
| N plugins on PATH, external_agents on | **N** |
| external_agents off, no `--all` | **0** — walk not run |

So the finding's numbers (9 plugins → 9 execs) are the "power user dropped 9 plugins on PATH" case. A normal user with none pays nothing.

## Why this reframes the two remaining levers
- **Parallelize**: still runs N probes, but concurrently → wall ≈ one probe (~90ms) instead of N×90ms. Cost stays N execs, wall drops.
- **Persist install-state**: cost = *installed* count, not PATH count. In the 1-of-9 case that's **1 exec, not 9** — the only lever that breaks the "scales with PATH plugin count" property.

So the choice sharpens: if the worry is "someone has many plugins on PATH but few installed," **persist** is the real fix (N→installed-count). If plugins-on-PATH ≈ installed anyway, **parallelize** is enough. Which matches your users better?

## Proposed semantics
- `entire agent list` → **built-ins only**. Zero external execs, zero PATH walk. Fast as main (~in-process built-in checks). This is the sub-100ms listing command staying fast.
- `entire agent list --external` → **externals only**, walk PATH + probe `are-hooks-installed`, mark installed vs available. Slower — but the user typed the flag, so the latency is expected and owned.

Why this resolves the finding cleanly: the perf problem was "a fast listing command silently does N execs." Move the N execs behind an opt-in flag and the default is never slow. The cost only exists when explicitly requested. Honest and simple.

## Cost table under this design
| command | external execs | speed |
|---|---|---|
| `list` (any user) | **0** | fast, always |
| `list --external`, N plugins on PATH | N | slow, opt-in |

## Decisions to nail down
1. **`--external` = externals only** (your words), not built-ins+externals. Two commands for the full picture — fine, and keeps the flag meaning crisp.
2. **Drop `--all`?** I'd replace `--all` with `--external` — `--all` currently means "built-ins + available externals," which overlaps confusingly. One flag, one job. (Reuses the existing `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` path.)

This also lets the default path drop `settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled` gating entirely for listing — default never touches externals regardless of the setting. `--external` can still honor or bypass the setting (I'd have `--external` always scan, since it's explicit).

Net: default `list` == main's speed, externals are one explicit flag away. Parallelize/persist become optional polish for the `--external` path only.
